items.name: RFA Checklist Extraction v2.0.1
items.description: Uploads a federal funding announcement (RFA, FOA, NOFO, or program solicitation) and returns a single RA-friendly Markdown checklist organized in the pre-award sections a sponsored-programs analyst uses when triaging an opportunity, led by a Red Flags section that surfaces escalation and contract-review triggers first: Red Flags, Dates & Deadlines, Eligibility, Award Information, Budget Requirements & Policies, Submission Details, Application Components, Compliance Risks, Foreign Influence & International Components, Special Requirements, and Important Notes. The pipeline runs ten parallel Prompt tasks (each emitting a JSON fragment for its block) plus a Consolidation Prompt that renders the final Markdown checklist with strict de-duplication. Mirrors the ui-insight/ProcessMapping rfa-checklist-extraction workflow's consolidated sections and placement contract, extended with the 2026-08 pre-award RA feedback (Red Flags, section reorder, recurring date resolution, richer eligibility) and a baked-in sponsor backbone that auto-includes each federal sponsor's standard required components and default formatting when the announcement omits them. v0.7.0 adds the expanded Red Flags / Contract-Review trigger set and Compliance Risks + Foreign Influence sections from the RA's SPA checklist.

data.name: extract-opportunity-metadata
data.prompt:
You are extracting the scalar OPPORTUNITY METADATA from a
federal funding announcement (RFA / FOA / NOFO / program
solicitation). You receive the full uploaded document as your
context. Read the entire document — cover page, header,
program description, sponsor information, instructions.

Extract these fields. Quote the document for every value;
never invent. Use null when the document does not state a
value.

- rfa_id: Combined sponsor-prefixed RFA identifier when both
  a sponsor code and opportunity number exist (e.g.,
  "NSF-26-508", "NIH-PA-24-246", "DOE-DE-FOA-0003117"). null
  otherwise.
- rfa_number: The sponsor's announcement number without
  agency prefix (e.g., "26-508", "PA-24-246",
  "DE-FOA-0003117").
- rfa_title: Full title of the funding opportunity, including
  any track or component designation. Required.
- sponsor_name: Full name of the lead sponsoring agency
  (e.g., "National Science Foundation"); never an
  abbreviation. Required.
- program_code: Sponsor's internal program or division code
  (e.g., "NSF/TIP/ITE"); null if not stated.
- announcement_url: Canonical URL of the announcement on the
  sponsor's site; null if not present.
- opportunity_number: Grants.gov or portal opportunity ID
  when distinct from rfa_number; null otherwise.
- cfda_number: CFDA / Assistance Listing number(s); when
  multiple, comma-separate (e.g., "47.070, 47.076").
- funding_instrument_type: The award mechanism as stated —
  "Grant", "Cooperative Agreement", "Contract", or another
  instrument the announcement names. Use the document's own
  term; null when it does not state one. Do NOT guess from the
  sponsor (e.g., do not assume "Grant" just because it is NSF).

## Output compactness (CRITICAL)

Your output feeds a downstream consolidation step and is never
read by a human. The runtime enforces a hard output-token cap on
this task — a verbose fragment gets cut off mid-string, which
destroys every field after the cut. Therefore:

- Emit MINIFIED JSON: one single line, no indentation, no
  newlines inside the JSON, no spaces after `:` or `,`.
- Minify the SYNTAX only — do NOT shorten, summarize, or drop
  content values. Every fact the schema asks for is still
  required, stated fully ("Up to $5M/year for 4 years, total not
  to exceed $20M" must NOT become "$20M total").
- Inside a JSON string value, escape any double quote as \"
  or rephrase using single quotes ('added value', not
  "added value") — one unescaped quote invalidates the
  entire fragment.
- Any JSON examples shown in this prompt are indented for
  readability only — YOUR output must be minified.

## Output

Emit exactly one JSON object with these nine keys. No
preamble, no closing commentary, no markdown fences. Example
shape:

{
  "rfa_id": "NSF-26-508",
  "rfa_number": "26-508",
  "rfa_title": "Mid-Scale Research Infrastructure-2 (Mid-scale RI-2)",
  "sponsor_name": "National Science Foundation",
  "program_code": "NSF/TIP",
  "announcement_url": "https://www.nsf.gov/funding/...",
  "opportunity_number": null,
  "cfda_number": "47.083",
  "funding_instrument_type": "Cooperative Agreement"
}

Begin your reply with the character `{` and emit NOTHING except
the single minified JSON object — no preamble, no questions, no
offers to help, no commentary, no markdown fences.

data.name: extract-risk-flags
data.prompt:
You are extracting the RED FLAGS block of a federal funding
announcement. You receive the full uploaded document as your
context. Read the ENTIRE document — eligibility, budget /
cost principles, submission instructions, required
attachments, terms and conditions, and any appendix — because
these triggers are frequently buried late or stated only
once.

A pre-award research administrator uses this block to decide,
within seconds of opening the report, whether this submission
needs a LONGER lead time, extra institutional routing, or
Contract Review Unit (CRU) review. Your job is to CHECK FOR
each known trigger below and report its status.

Assess EACH of the fixed checks. Ground every determination in
the document — quote or paraphrase the triggering language in
`detail`. NEVER assert a trigger the document does not support;
when the document does not address a check, use status
"unclear" (not "no"). Use "no" only when the document
affirmatively indicates the trigger does not apply (e.g., "No
cost sharing is required", "Indirect costs are permitted at the
negotiated rate"). Accuracy matters more than completeness —
the RA would rather see "unclear" than a fabricated flag.

The checks fall in two groups. Tag each with `category`.

### Group 1 — Escalation flags (category: "escalation")
Items that lengthen the process or require early institutional
action:

- "Cost share / matching required" — any required or mandatory
  cost share, matching, or in-kind contribution.
- "F&A / indirect limited or waived" — indirect (F&A) rate
  capped, reduced, disallowed, or a waiver required (e.g.,
  "indirect costs limited to 10%", "no F&A permitted").
- "Institutional / executive commitment letter" — a required
  letter of commitment or support that must be signed above the
  PI: institutional, presidential, provost / vice-provost,
  dean, or chair letter.
- "Limited submission" — the sponsor caps how many proposals
  the INSTITUTION may submit or how many an INDIVIDUAL may be
  named on. Capture the number in `detail`.
- "Documents requiring signature / institution must submit" —
  an Authorized Organizational Representative (AOR) or
  institutional-official signature is required, and/or the
  proposal must be submitted by the institution rather than the
  PI directly.

### Group 2 — Contract Review Unit (CRU) triggers (category: "cru")
Terms and conditions that require CRU review BEFORE submission.
Any one of these that is "yes" means the proposal and/or its
terms must be routed to the Contract Review Officer (via VERAS
Correspondence) before submission:

- "Indemnification" — indemnify-and-hold-harmless or similar
  liability-assumption language.
- "Intellectual property / data ownership restrictions" —
  sponsor claims on IP, invention rights, or data ownership.
- "Publication restrictions" — limits on the right to publish
  or approval/embargo of publications.
- "Insurance requirements" — the sponsor requires the
  institution to carry specific insurance.
- "Nondisclosure agreement (NDA)" — an NDA or confidentiality
  agreement is required.
- "FAR-based or contract-type terms" — the award is a contract
  or references / is subject to the Federal Acquisition
  Regulation (FAR); procurement/bid-type assistance.
- "Governing law of another state" — the agreement is governed
  by the law of a state other than Idaho (e.g., Louisiana).
- "Acceptance of terms & conditions upon submission" — any
  language stating that submitting the proposal constitutes
  acceptance of the sponsor's terms and conditions.
- "Restricted country / foreign ownership" — involvement of
  entities, collaborators, or subrecipients in China, Russia,
  North Korea, or Iran, including foreign-owned corporations
  based in those countries (e.g., Syngenta).
- "Foreign government or national-lab contracting" — an
  all-Canadian-Government proposal, or contracting with Idaho
  National Laboratory (INL) or the Jet Propulsion Laboratory
  (JPL) (scope review / draft contracts).
- "Controlled unclassified information (CUI) or classified
  information" — the project involves CUI or classified
  information exchange.
- "Other unusual terms and conditions" — any other atypical
  term that a contract reviewer would need to see. Only when
  document-supported; otherwise "unclear".

For EACH check emit an object with these four keys:

- check: the exact label from the lists above. Required.
- category: "escalation" or "cru", per the group. Required.
- status: one of "yes", "no", "unclear". Required.
- detail: when status is "yes", a short grounded phrase naming
  the trigger and its specifics (amount, percentage, count, who
  signs, which country/entity, the clause). When "no", a brief
  note of the affirming statement. When "unclear", null.
  Preserve the sponsor's monetary / percentage formatting
  verbatim.

You may ALSO append additional objects for any OTHER
document-supported condition that would clearly lengthen the
process or require early institutional action (e.g., "Required
travel to a sponsor meeting"). Give those a descriptive `check`
label, the best-fit `category`, and status "yes". Do not
manufacture these — only add what the document supports.

## Output compactness (CRITICAL)

Your output feeds a downstream consolidation step and is never
read by a human. The runtime enforces a hard output-token cap on
this task — a verbose fragment gets cut off mid-string, which
destroys every field after the cut. Therefore:

- Emit MINIFIED JSON: one single line, no indentation, no
  newlines inside the JSON, no spaces after `:` or `,`.
- Minify the SYNTAX only — do NOT shorten, summarize, or drop
  content values. Every fact the schema asks for is still
  required, stated fully ("Up to $5M/year for 4 years, total not
  to exceed $20M" must NOT become "$20M total").
- Inside a JSON string value, escape any double quote as \"
  or rephrase using single quotes ('added value', not
  "added value") — one unescaped quote invalidates the
  entire fragment.
- Any JSON examples shown in this prompt are indented for
  readability only — YOUR output must be minified.

## Output

Emit exactly one JSON object with one key, `risk_flags`, whose
value is a JSON array containing one object per fixed check (in
the order listed) plus any additional supported flags. No
preamble, no markdown fences. Example:

{
  "risk_flags": [
    {"check": "Cost share / matching required", "category": "escalation", "status": "yes", "detail": "1:1 non-federal match of the total award required"},
    {"check": "F&A / indirect limited or waived", "category": "escalation", "status": "yes", "detail": "Indirect costs limited to 10% of total direct costs"},
    {"check": "Institutional / executive commitment letter", "category": "escalation", "status": "unclear", "detail": null},
    {"check": "Limited submission", "category": "escalation", "status": "yes", "detail": "Maximum of two proposals per institution"},
    {"check": "Documents requiring signature / institution must submit", "category": "escalation", "status": "yes", "detail": "Must be submitted via Research.gov by the institution's AOR"},
    {"check": "Indemnification", "category": "cru", "status": "yes", "detail": "Recipient must indemnify and hold the sponsor harmless (Section 12)"},
    {"check": "Publication restrictions", "category": "cru", "status": "no", "detail": "No publication approval or embargo stated"},
    {"check": "Acceptance of terms & conditions upon submission", "category": "cru", "status": "yes", "detail": "Submission constitutes acceptance of the sponsor's terms"}
  ]
}

Begin your reply with the character `{` and emit NOTHING except
the single minified JSON object — no preamble, no questions, no
offers to help, no commentary, no markdown fences.

data.name: extract-dates-and-deadlines
data.prompt:
You are extracting the DATES & DEADLINES block of a federal
funding announcement. You receive the full uploaded document
as your context. Search every section of the document
including the main body, appendices, footnotes, sidebar
callouts.

Extract every unique date or time-bound event in the
announcement. For multi-round solicitations include every
round's LOI, pre-proposal, and full proposal deadlines.

RESOLVE RECURRING / RELATIVE DEADLINES. Sponsors (especially
NSF) often state a deadline as a rule rather than a calendar
date — e.g., "the second Tuesday in September", "the fourth
Thursday of each October", "the first business day of the
fiscal year", or a standing deadline that "recurs annually
until 2027". When a deadline is expressed this way:
- COMPUTE the concrete calendar date it resolves to and put
  that ISO date in `date_time` (e.g., a rule of "second Tuesday
  in September 2026" resolves to "2026-09-08").
- Resolve the NEXT upcoming occurrence relative to the
  announcement's own dates. If the rule recurs and the
  document names an end year, you may list the next occurrence
  in `date_time` and describe the recurrence in `notes` (or
  emit one row per upcoming occurrence when only a few remain).
- ALWAYS record the ORIGINAL rule text in `notes` (e.g.,
  "Sponsor states: second Tuesday in September; recurs annually
  through 2027") so the RA can verify the computation.
This resolution is pure date arithmetic on a rule the document
states explicitly — it is NOT invention. Do NOT guess or
fabricate a date the document does not define. If a rule is
genuinely ambiguous (no year or anchor to compute from), leave
`date_time` as the rule text and explain in `notes`.

For each date emit an object with these three keys:

- item: The event label exactly as stated in the document
  (e.g., "Letter of Intent Due", "Full Proposal Deadline",
  "Award Notification"). Required.
- date_time: Full date plus any time and timezone as
  published (e.g., "2026-09-15 5:00 PM ET", "2026-10-01",
  "Rolling"). For a recurring / relative rule, the RESOLVED
  concrete date (see above). Preserve the sponsor's granularity
  exactly for absolute dates. Do not invent precision. Required.
- notes: Any conditions, round identifiers, or clarifications
  attached to this date (e.g., "Track 1 only", "Optional but
  encouraged"), AND — for any resolved recurring / relative
  deadline — the original rule text the date was computed from.
  null when none.

## Output compactness (CRITICAL)

Your output feeds a downstream consolidation step and is never
read by a human. The runtime enforces a hard output-token cap on
this task — a verbose fragment gets cut off mid-string, which
destroys every field after the cut. Therefore:

- Emit MINIFIED JSON: one single line, no indentation, no
  newlines inside the JSON, no spaces after `:` or `,`.
- Minify the SYNTAX only — do NOT shorten, summarize, or drop
  content values. Every fact the schema asks for is still
  required, stated fully ("Up to $5M/year for 4 years, total not
  to exceed $20M" must NOT become "$20M total").
- Inside a JSON string value, escape any double quote as \"
  or rephrase using single quotes ('added value', not
  "added value") — one unescaped quote invalidates the
  entire fragment.
- Any JSON examples shown in this prompt are indented for
  readability only — YOUR output must be minified.

## Output

Emit exactly one JSON object with one key,
`dates_and_deadlines`, whose value is a JSON array of date
objects sorted chronologically. No preamble, no markdown
fences. Example:

{
  "dates_and_deadlines": [
    {"item": "Letter of Intent Due", "date_time": "2026-08-01 5:00 PM ET", "notes": "Required for full proposal eligibility"},
    {"item": "Full Proposal Deadline", "date_time": "2026-09-08 5:00 PM ET", "notes": "Resolved from sponsor rule: second Tuesday in September; recurs annually through 2027"}
  ]
}

Begin your reply with the character `{` and emit NOTHING except
the single minified JSON object — no preamble, no questions, no
offers to help, no commentary, no markdown fences.

data.name: extract-eligible-institutions
data.prompt:
You are extracting the ELIGIBLE INSTITUTIONS subsection of a
federal funding announcement. You receive the full uploaded
document as your context. Read the eligibility section, any
appendix or attached eligibility guidance, and any sponsor
terms-and-conditions referenced inline.

List every distinct institution category the sponsor names.
Put institutional prerequisites (SAM.gov registration,
domestic-only restrictions, A-133 audit status) in
compliance_requirements. Do NOT put PI-level rules here —
those belong to extract-eligible-individuals.

EXPLICITLY look for and capture, when stated:
- LIMITED SUBMISSION caps at the INSTITUTION level — e.g., "an
  institution may submit no more than two proposals". Record
  the exact number in compliance_requirements (and it will
  also surface in Red Flags).
- Required institutional CERTIFICATIONS / CREDENTIALS or
  special status — e.g., Carnegie classification, EPSCoR
  jurisdiction, minority-serving-institution status, a required
  accreditation or registration.
- SUBRECIPIENT / SUBAWARDEE eligibility, when the announcement
  states rules specific to subrecipients (domestic-only,
  foreign-subrecipient restrictions, industry-participation
  rules, nonprofit requirements, tribal eligibility). Emit
  these as a SEPARATE entry with type "Subrecipients /
  Subawardees" and the rules in compliance_requirements. Only
  when the document states subrecipient-specific rules — do not
  fabricate this entry.

Include ONLY categories and rules the announcement actually
states; never infer an institution type or restriction that is
not in the document.

For each institution category emit an object with these four
keys:

- type: Institution category label as stated (e.g.,
  "Institutions of Higher Education", "Nonprofit
  Organizations Other Than Institutions of Higher Education",
  "Small Businesses"). Required.
- subcategory: More specific classification when given (e.g.,
  "R1 research universities", "HBCUs", "EPSCoR-eligible").
  null when the type has no subcategorization.
- examples: Sponsor-supplied examples that illustrate the
  category, as a short comma-separated list. null when the
  announcement gives none.
- compliance_requirements: Registrations, certifications,
  institutional prerequisites, or institution-level
  limited-submission caps attached to this type (e.g.,
  "SAM.gov registration required", "Maximum of two proposals
  per institution"). null when no institutional compliance
  terms are attached.

## Output compactness (CRITICAL)

Your output feeds a downstream consolidation step and is never
read by a human. The runtime enforces a hard output-token cap on
this task — a verbose fragment gets cut off mid-string, which
destroys every field after the cut. Therefore:

- Emit MINIFIED JSON: one single line, no indentation, no
  newlines inside the JSON, no spaces after `:` or `,`.
- Minify the SYNTAX only — do NOT shorten, summarize, or drop
  content values. Every fact the schema asks for is still
  required, stated fully ("Up to $5M/year for 4 years, total not
  to exceed $20M" must NOT become "$20M total").
- Inside a JSON string value, escape any double quote as \"
  or rephrase using single quotes ('added value', not
  "added value") — one unescaped quote invalidates the
  entire fragment.
- Any JSON examples shown in this prompt are indented for
  readability only — YOUR output must be minified.

## Output

Emit exactly one JSON object with one key,
`eligible_institutions`, whose value is a JSON array. MUST
be non-empty — if truly nothing is stated, emit a single
entry with type "Not specified in this document". No
preamble, no markdown fences.

Begin your reply with the character `{` and emit NOTHING except
the single minified JSON object — no preamble, no questions, no
offers to help, no commentary, no markdown fences.

data.name: extract-eligible-individuals
data.prompt:
You are extracting the ELIGIBLE INDIVIDUALS subsection of a
federal funding announcement. You receive the full uploaded
document as your context. Read the eligibility section and
any PI-eligibility appendix.

List every distinct PI / Co-PI / Senior Key Personnel
category the sponsor names. Include citizenship,
career-stage, degree, appointment type, and prior-award
restrictions in criteria or conditions.

EXPLICITLY look for and capture, when stated:
- CITIZENSHIP / residency requirements (e.g., "U.S. citizen or
  permanent resident required").
- CAREER-STAGE restrictions — early-career / new-investigator
  limits, years-since-degree windows, "no prior R01", etc.
- Required CERTIFICATIONS or CREDENTIALS the individual must
  hold (e.g., a terminal degree, a license, a specific title
  or tenured/tenure-track appointment).
- LIMITED SUBMISSION caps at the INDIVIDUAL level — how many
  proposals a person may be named on / submit (e.g., "an
  investigator may appear on only one proposal"). Record the
  exact number. Institution-wide caps ("one nomination per
  institution") belong in conditions here (and also surface in
  Red Flags), NOT in Special Requirements.
- LIMITED-SUBMISSION MECHANICS when stated — how collaborative
  proposals count toward a cap, and any required internal
  institutional nomination / down-select competition. Put these
  in conditions.

Capture ONLY what the announcement states; never infer a cap,
a citizenship rule, or a nomination process the document does
not give. When an item is not addressed, omit it rather than
guessing.

For each individual category emit an object with these four
keys:

- type: Individual eligibility category (e.g., "Principal
  Investigator", "Early-Career Investigator",
  "Co-Investigator"). Required.
- criteria: Qualifying criteria (degree, career stage,
  appointment type, citizenship, required credentials); null
  when none.
- compliance_requirements: ORCID, mentoring plans, or other
  PI compliance items; null when none.
- conditions: Restrictions, limits, or preferences, including

  "One nomination per institution", "May appear on only one

  none.

Your output feeds a downstream consolidation step and is never

this task — a verbose fragment gets cut off mid-string, which
destroys every field after the cut. Therefore:

- Emit MINIFIED JSON: one single line, no indentation, no

- Minify the SYNTAX only — do NOT shorten, summarize, or drop
  content values. Every fact the schema asks for is still
  required, stated fully ("Up to $5M/year for 4 years, total not
  to exceed $20M" must NOT become "$20M total").
- Inside a JSON string value, escape any double quote as \"
  or rephrase using single quotes ('added value', not
  "added value") — one unescaped quote invalidates the
  entire fragment.
- Any JSON examples shown in this prompt are indented for
  readability only — YOUR output must be minified.

## Output

Emit exactly one JSON object with one key,
`eligible_individuals`, whose value is a JSON array. MUST be
non-empty — if truly nothing is stated, emit a single entry
with type "Not specified in this document". No preamble, no
markdown fences.

the single minified JSON object — no preamble, no questions, no
offers to help, no commentary, no markdown fences.

data.name: extract-award-information
data.prompt:
You are extracting the AWARD INFORMATION block of a federal
funding announcement. You receive the full uploaded document
as your context. Read the award-information section, program
description, and any appendix that states funding amounts.

This block is the SOLE location for primary award parameters
in the final deliverable — do NOT capture detailed financial
rules (those belong to extract-budget-requirements).

Ground every value in the document. NEVER invent an amount,
duration, count, or date, and NEVER infer a "typical" figure
from the program or sponsor. Preserve the sponsor's exact
numeric formatting. When the announcement does not state a
value, use the string "Not specified in the document" for

Extract these four fields:

- award_duration: Anticipated duration exactly as stated (e.g.,

data.name: extract-application-components
data.prompt:
You are extracting the APPLICATION COMPONENTS, SUBMISSION
DETAILS, SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS, and FORMATTING REQUIREMENTS
blocks of a federal funding announcement. You receive the full
uploaded document. Read every section that describes what to
submit and how to submit it.

A SEPARATE parallel task extracts the announcement-mandated
INTERNAL structure of components (e.g., required Project
Description sections). Do NOT enumerate internal section
structure here. A component's special_requirements carries ONLY
page limits, title rules, fonts, templates, and naming — never
"must include the sections in Section V.A"-style pointers.

Placement rules: per-component rules (page limits, fonts,
templates, naming) go in that component's special_requirements.
Portal / file-format / upload mechanics go in
submission_details. Document-wide preparation rules (fonts,
margins, spacing, page size, file naming) go in
formatting_requirements.

## Sponsor backbone — ALWAYS include the standard components

Federal sponsors often do NOT list every required proposal
component in an individual announcement — some are standardized
in the sponsor's proposal guide (e.g., the NSF PAPPG). You MUST
still include them:

1. Identify the sponsor. Hints: "National Science Foundation" /
   "NSF 25-543" → NSF; "National Institutes of Health" / "PA-",
   "PAR-", "RFA-", "NOT-" → NIH; "USDA" / "NIFA" → USDA-NIFA;
   "Department of Energy" / "DE-FOA-" → DOE; "NASA" / "NNH",
   "NRA" → NASA.
2. MERGE that sponsor's standard components (backbone below)
   with what the announcement states. Unconditional backbone
   items → required_components; "(if applicable)" items →
   optional_components. If the announcement also names a
   component, emit ONE entry using the announcement's wording
   and rules. If the announcement modifies a standard component
   (page limit, extra content), keep the change on the
   component.
3. Set each component's `source`: "Announcement" (announcement
   requires it, not a backbone item), "Sponsor standard" (added
   from the backbone), or "Announcement + sponsor standard"
   (present in both, or backbone item the announcement
   modifies).
4. "Subaward Documents (if applicable)" is a conditional
   OPTIONAL component: list it with its standard sub-items
   (Budget (excel); RR Subaward Budget form if applicable;
   Budget Justification; Senior Key Personnel Documents —
   sponsor SciENcv Biosketch + Current & Pending; Specific
   Scope of Work; AOR-signed Letter of Commitment if on the FDP
   list, or a completed UI subrecipient Commitment form;
   Facilities/Equipment if applicable) in its description.
5. If the sponsor is NOT one of the five below, DO NOT invent a
   backbone — extract only what the announcement states; every
   `source` is "Announcement".

### Backbone — standard required components by sponsor

- NSF: Project Summary; Project Description; References Cited;
  Budget; Budget Justification; Facilities, Equipment & Other
  Resources; Biographical Sketch (SciENcv); Current & Pending
  Support (SciENcv); Collaborators & Other Affiliations (COA);
  Synergistic Activities; Data Management & Sharing Plan;
  Mentoring Plan (if applicable); Other Supplementary Documents

  Subaward Documents (if applicable).
- NIH: Project Summary/Abstract; Project Narrative; Bibliography
  & References Cited; Facilities & Other Resources; Equipment;
  Biographical Sketches (SciENcv, all key personnel); Budget;
  Budget Justification; Introduction to Application
  [Resubmission/Revision] (if applicable); Specific Aims;
  Research Strategy; Data Management and Sharing Plan; Vertebrate
  Animals Section (if applicable); Select Agent Research (if
  applicable); Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan (if applicable);
  Consortium/Contractual Arrangements (if applicable); Letters
  of Collaboration (if applicable); Human Subjects/Clinical
  Trial documents (if applicable); Resource Sharing Plan(s) (if
  applicable); Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical
  Resources.
- USDA-NIFA: Project Summary; Project Narrative; Budget; Budget
  Justification; Biographical Sketches (SciENcv); Current &
  Pending Support (SciENcv); Conflict of Interest List;
  Bibliography & References Cited; Facilities and Other
  Resources; Equipment; Data Management Plan (if applicable);
  Mentoring Plan (if applicable); Logic Model (if applicable);
  Key Personnel Roles (if applicable); Management Plan (if
  applicable); Documentation of Collaboration (if applicable);
  Subaward Documents (if applicable).
- DOE: Project Summary/Abstract; Project Narrative; Statement of
  Work; Budget; Budget Justification; Biographical Sketches
  (SciENcv); Current & Pending Support (SciENcv); Facilities &
  Other Resources; Equipment; Data Management and Sharing Plan
  (if applicable); Letters of Collaboration/Commitment (if
  applicable); Subaward Documents (if applicable).
- NASA: Proposal Summary/Abstract;
  Scientific/Technical/Management Plan; References Cited; Budget;
  Budget Justification; Biographical Sketches (SciENcv); Current
  & Pending Support (SciENcv); Facilities, Equipment & Other
  Resources; Table of Personnel and Work Effort; Data Management
  Plan (if applicable); Letters of Commitment/Support (if
  applicable); Subaward Documents (if applicable). Senior Key
  Personnel documents apply to PI/Co-PI/Co-I with ≥10% effort/yr.

## Formatting precedence (fills formatting_requirements)

If the announcement gives SPECIFIC formatting instructions, use
those verbatim. If it is silent, populate from the sponsor
default below prefixed exactly with "Sponsor default
(<SPONSOR>):". If it gives some rules but not others, combine:
stated rules first, then note the sponsor default fills the
rest. Non-backbone sponsor with no stated formatting → null.

### Backbone — sponsor-standard formatting

- NSF: Fonts — Arial (not narrow), Courier New, or Palatino
  Linotype at 10pt+, or Times New Roman / Computer Modern 11pt+.
  Margins ≥1 inch all sides (incl. headers/footers). Line
  spacing ≤6 lines/inch. Page size 8.5×11 in.
- NIH: Font 11pt+ (smaller allowed only in graphics if legible
  at 100%). Type density ≤15 characters/inch. Line spacing ≤6
  lines/inch. Recommended black font (Arial, Georgia, Helvetica,
  Palatino Linotype). File names ≤50 characters. No URLs except
  citations in References Cited and Biosketch. No headers or
  footers.
- USDA-NIFA: Typed/word-processed. Font ≥12pt regardless of line
  spacing. Margins ≥1 inch. Number pages sequentially (unless
  via eRA). PDF format. File names ≤50 characters, no special
  characters (& – * % / #), periods, spaces, or accents;
  underscores allowed; names must be unique.
- DOE: Defer to the NOFO/FOA; otherwise 8.5×11 in, 1-inch
  margins, font 11pt+, PDF, avoid URLs with substantive content
  unless the FOA permits.
- NASA: 8.5×11 in, ≥1-inch margins, single-spaced 12pt, one
  column, page limits per the NOFO; only non-substantive
  material in headers/footers.

- required_components: array of {name, description,
  special_requirements, source} (backbone-merged). MUST be
  non-empty. description uses the announcement's terms;
  special_requirements is null when none, and NEVER a pointer to
  an announcement section.
- optional_components: same shape; empty array when none.
  Backbone "(if applicable)" items and Subaward Documents live
  here.
- submission_details: one coherent paragraph — submission
  method/portal (NAME the system the announcement states, e.g.
  Grants.gov, Research.gov, eRA Commons, JustGrants, NSPIRES,
  ProposalCentral; never guess), file formats, naming,
  collaboration rules. null only if no submission guidance at
  all.
- special_requirements: array of strings — unique RFA aspects
  that fit no other section (conference travel obligations,
  data-sharing beyond federal defaults, workshop participation).
  Empty array when none.
- formatting_requirements: string per the precedence rule above,
  or null.

## Output compactness (CRITICAL)

Your output feeds a downstream consolidation step and is never
read by a human. The runtime enforces a hard output-token cap —
a verbose fragment gets cut off mid-string, destroying every
field after the cut. Therefore:

- Emit MINIFIED JSON: one single line, no indentation, no
  newlines inside the JSON, no spaces after `:` or `,`.
- Minify the SYNTAX only — do NOT shorten, summarize, or drop
  content values.
- Inside a JSON string value, escape any double quote as \"
  or rephrase using single quotes — one unescaped quote
  invalidates the entire fragment.
- Emit the five keys in this order: submission_details,
  formatting_requirements, special_requirements,
  required_components, optional_components — cheap scalar fields
  first so they survive if the cap is hit.
- Within required_components, list "Announcement"-sourced
  components FIRST, then the backbone.
- BACKBONE STUBS: for a pure "Sponsor standard" component emit
  ONLY {"name":"...","source":"Sponsor standard"} — omit
  description and special_requirements. A stub costs ~60
  characters, so there is NO output-budget reason to drop the
  backbone. Emitting only the announcement-named components with
  the backbone missing is an extraction failure — every backbone
  item must be present as a stub.
- OMIT any component key whose value would be null. Never omit
  name or source.

## Output

Emit exactly one JSON object with these five keys. Begin your
reply with the character `{` and emit NOTHING except the single
minified JSON object — no preamble, no questions, no offers to
help, no commentary, no markdown fences.

data.name: extract-mandated-structure
data.prompt:
You are extracting the ANNOUNCEMENT-MANDATED INTERNAL STRUCTURE
of proposal components from a federal funding announcement. You
receive the full uploaded document.

Announcements frequently prescribe named sections that must
appear INSIDE a single proposal component — most often the
Project Description / Project Narrative. Trigger language looks
like: "All proposals should clearly include sections for each of
the following aspects:", "The Project Description must contain
the following sections", or a solicitation-specific supplement
to the sponsor's proposal guide (e.g., NSF's "The following
information supplements the guidelines and requirements in the
NSF PAPPG"). These enumerations are decision-critical: a
proposal missing a mandated section can be returned without
review, and the checklist reader does NOT have the announcement
open.

## Rules

1. For each component whose internal structure the announcement
   prescribes, emit one entry: {"component": "<component
   name>", "mandated_sections": [...]} — one mandated_sections
   item per mandated section, in the announcement's order,
   section names verbatim.
2. Each mandated_sections item is {name, requirements,
   subsections}. requirements: what the section must contain,
   in the announcement's terms, 30 words or fewer — compress
   the wording, never drop a named item.
3. When a mandated section itself has enumerated sub-parts
   (numbered sub-sections, a required table with named columns,
   a milestone list), capture EACH sub-part in that entry's
   `subsections` array ({name, requirements}); enumerate
   required table columns and named milestones fully (compact
   forms fine: "Alpha release ≤1 yr"). Omit `subsections` when
   there are none.
4. NEVER compress an enumeration into a pointer such as "must
   include all subsections listed in Section V.A". A pointer in
   place of the enumerated list is an extraction failure.
5. Only structure THIS announcement prescribes. Do NOT invent
   structure from the sponsor's standard proposal guide. If no
   component has announcement-mandated structure, emit
   {"mandated_structure":[]}.

## Worked example

An NSF solicitation states "All PCL Node proposals should
clearly include sections for each of the following aspects:"
followed by named sections.

WRONG (pointer prose, structure lost): a components entry whose
special_requirements says "Must include all specified
subsections listed in Section V.A" and no structure emitted.

CORRECT (abbreviated here — emit EVERY section the announcement
names, in order):

{"mandated_structure":[{"component":"Project Description",
"mandated_sections":[
{"name":"Science drivers","requirements":"Science drivers
driving Node development; identified users/communities; how
capabilities transform the science; impact on U.S.
competitiveness/security."},
{"name":"Node capabilities","requirements":"What makes the Node
capable/unique in supporting the science drivers.",
"subsections":[
{"name":"Instrument Inventory Table","requirements":"Separate
document, NOT in the 20-page limit; per instrument: type/
description + count; relevance with example workflows;
available time (duty cycle, hours/day)."},
{"name":"Node Expertise","requirements":"Team and expertise for
science drivers and data/AI issues."}]},
{"name":"Management Plan","requirements":"Roles of PI/co-PIs/
staff; coordination meetings.","subsections":[
{"name":"Implementation Timeline","requirements":"Milestones:
Project Kickoff; Alpha ≤1 yr; Beta ≤1.5 yr; Robust User Service
≤2 yr; Test Bed 2.0; Project end (Yr 4) deployment plan."}]}
]}]}

(The example is line-wrapped for readability only — YOUR output
must be one single minified line, and must include every
mandated section, not just the three shown.)

## Output compactness (CRITICAL)

Your output feeds a downstream consolidation step and is never
read by a human; the runtime enforces a hard output-token cap.
Emit MINIFIED JSON — one single line, no indentation, no spaces
after `:` or `,`. Minify the syntax only, never the content:
every named section, sub-part, table column, and milestone must
appear. When quoting announcement text inside a JSON string
value, escape any double quote as \" or rephrase using single
quotes ('added value', not "added value") — one unescaped
quote invalidates the entire fragment.

## Output

Emit exactly one JSON object with the single key
`mandated_structure` (array; empty array when the announcement
mandates no internal structure). Begin your reply with the
character `{` and emit NOTHING except the single minified JSON
object — no preamble, no questions, no offers to help, no
commentary, no markdown fences.

data.name: extract-compliance-flags
data.prompt:
You are extracting the COMPLIANCE RISKS and INTERNATIONAL
COMPONENTS blocks of a federal funding announcement. You
receive the full uploaded document as your context. Read the
entire document — program description, eligibility, submission
and reporting requirements, terms and conditions, and any
appendix — because these obligations are often stated once and
drive additional institutional review (IRB, IACUC, IBC, export
control, research security).

Assess EACH fixed area below. Ground every determination in the
document; put the triggering language in `detail`. NEVER assert
an obligation the document does not support — when the document
does not address an area, use status "unclear" (not "no"). Use
"no" only when the document affirmatively excludes it (e.g.,
"Human subjects research is not permitted under this program").
Accuracy over completeness: prefer "unclear" to a guess.

For every area emit an object with these keys:
- area: the exact label from the lists below. Required.
- status: "yes" (the announcement invokes / requires / restricts
  it), "no" (affirmatively excluded), or "unclear" (not
  addressed). Required.
- detail: when "yes", a short grounded phrase with specifics;
  when "no", the affirming statement; when "unclear", null.

## compliance_risks — fixed areas (research-compliance)

- "Human subjects" — human-subjects research / IRB review /
  clinical-trial requirements.
- "Vertebrate animals" — animal use / IACUC review.
- "Biosafety" — recombinant DNA, biohazards, Institutional
  Biosafety Committee review.
- "Export control" — export-control implications (ITAR / EAR),
  fundamental-research exclusion questions.
- "Select agents / dual-use research" — select-agent research or
  dual-use research of concern (DURC).
- "Controlled unclassified information (CUI)" — CUI generation,
  handling, or marking requirements. (Also flagged as a Contract
  Review trigger in Red Flags when classified exchange is
  involved.)
- "Data security / cybersecurity" — data-security or
  cybersecurity controls (e.g., NIST SP 800-171, CMMC, a
  System Security Plan).
- "National security" — national-security considerations or
  restrictions stated by the sponsor.

## international_components — fixed areas (foreign influence)

- "Foreign collaborators" — whether foreign collaborators /
  personnel are allowed, required, or restricted.
- "Foreign subawards" — whether foreign subawards / subrecipients
  are allowed or restricted.
- "Foreign travel" — foreign-travel allowances or restrictions.
- "Foreign talent-program certification" — required
  certification or disclosure regarding malign foreign talent
  recruitment programs.
- "International data sharing" — restrictions on sharing data or
  materials internationally.
- "Country-specific restrictions" — restrictions tied to
  specific countries (e.g., prohibitions on China, Russia, North
  Korea, Iran, or their entities). (Also flagged as a Contract
  Review trigger in Red Flags.)

## Output compactness (CRITICAL)

Your output feeds a downstream consolidation step and is never
read by a human. The runtime enforces a hard output-token cap on
this task — a verbose fragment gets cut off mid-string, which
destroys every field after the cut. Therefore:

- Emit MINIFIED JSON: one single line, no indentation, no
  newlines inside the JSON, no spaces after `:` or `,`.
- Minify the SYNTAX only — do NOT shorten, summarize, or drop
  content values. Every fact the schema asks for is still
  required, stated fully ("Up to $5M/year for 4 years, total not
  to exceed $20M" must NOT become "$20M total").
- Inside a JSON string value, escape any double quote as \"
  or rephrase using single quotes ('added value', not
  "added value") — one unescaped quote invalidates the
  entire fragment.
- Any JSON examples shown in this prompt are indented for
  readability only — YOUR output must be minified.

## Output

Emit exactly one JSON object with two keys, `compliance_risks`
and `international_components`, each a JSON array with one object
per fixed area in the order listed. No preamble, no markdown
fences. Example:

{
  "compliance_risks": [
    {"area": "Human subjects", "status": "yes", "detail": "Involves human subjects; IRB approval required before award"},
    {"area": "Vertebrate animals", "status": "no", "detail": "Program excludes animal research"},
    {"area": "Export control", "status": "unclear", "detail": null}
  ],
  "international_components": [
    {"area": "Foreign subawards", "status": "no", "detail": "Foreign subawards are not permitted under this NOFO"},

data.name: rfa-checklist-consolidation
data.prompt:
You are the consolidation step of the RFA Checklist
Extraction workflow. You receive TEN JSON object fragments
from the previous step. Fragments arrive as MINIFIED JSON;
keys may appear in any order, and an object may OMIT a key
whose value would be null (treat a missing key exactly as
null):

1. Opportunity metadata (rfa_id, rfa_number, rfa_title,
   sponsor_name, program_code, announcement_url,
   opportunity_number, cfda_number, funding_instrument_type)
2. Risk flags (risk_flags: array of {check, category, status,
   detail}; category is "escalation" or "cru")
3. Dates and deadlines (array of {item, date_time, notes})
4. Eligible institutions (array of {type, subcategory,
   examples, compliance_requirements})
5. Eligible individuals (array of {type, criteria,
   compliance_requirements, conditions})
6. Award information (award_duration, amount_per_award,
   number_of_awards, anticipated_award_date)
7. Application components (required_components,
   optional_components, submission_details,
   special_requirements, formatting_requirements) — component
   objects carry a `source` field (Announcement / Sponsor
   standard / Announcement + sponsor standard) marking
   backbone provenance. Pure "Sponsor standard" components
   arrive as STUBS: {name, source} only
8. Budget requirements (funding_limits, cost_sharing_status,
   cost_sharing_details, fa_policy, allowable_costs,
   unallowable_costs, personnel_effort, other_considerations)
9. Compliance & international (compliance_risks: array of
   {area, status, detail}; international_components: array of
   {area, status, detail})
10. Mandated structure (mandated_structure: array of
   {component, mandated_sections}; each mandated_sections
   item is {name, requirements, subsections?} enumerating
   internal sections the announcement mandates for that
   component)

Your job is to render a single, well-formatted Markdown
checklist for the sponsored-programs analyst (the
end-user). The deliverable is Markdown — NOT a JSON object
and NOT a JSON code fence. The audience is a research
administrator who will copy this into Word, paste into an
email to the proposal team, or save to a shared folder.

## CRITICAL — ALWAYS RENDER THE DELIVERABLE

You MUST render the FULL Markdown deliverable structure (every
section listed below), EVEN WHEN some fragment fields arrive
as null, empty, missing, or sparse. NEVER refuse to render
with apologetic prose like "The provided context does not
contain the required information." That output is unusable —
the operator needs the full structure with placeholders so
they can see which fields need to be chased.

If a fragment arrives as truncated or malformed JSON (cut
off mid-string by an upstream output cap), do NOT discard
it — salvage every field and array entry that parses, and
treat everything after the cut as missing.

Substitution rules when a field is null or missing:
- Required scalar fields: substitute the literal string
  "Not specified in the document".
- Optional table cells: substitute "—" (em dash).
- Empty arrays: render the section with its empty-state
  language already specified below (e.g., "No items identified",
  "Defers to federal defaults", "None identified beyond
  standard federal requirements").

If EVERY field across ALL upstream fragments is null (which
means the document genuinely contained nothing extractable
OR the document was not attached to the run), STILL render
the full Markdown structure with "Not specified in the
document" placeholders throughout, AND append a single line
at the very end of the deliverable:

> ⚠️ The upstream extraction returned no data from the
> uploaded document. Verify the document was attached and
> re-run the workflow.

## Required structure (in this exact order)

# RFA Checklist: <rfa_title>

**Sponsor:** <sponsor_name>
**RFA ID / Number:** <rfa_id> / <rfa_number>
**Program Code:** <program_code or "Not specified">
**Announcement URL:** <announcement_url or "Not specified">
**Opportunity Number:** <opportunity_number or "Not specified">
**CFDA Number:** <cfda_number or "Not specified">
**Funding Instrument:** <funding_instrument_type or "Not specified">

---

## ⚠️ RED FLAGS

The FIRST thing the reviewer reads. Surface the triggers that
make this submission higher-effort, longer-lead-time, or in
need of Contract Review Unit review, so the RA can start the
long-pole processes early. Build this section from the RISK
FLAGS fragment (fragment 2), which tags each check with a
`category` of "escalation" or "cru". Render two subgroups; show
ONLY checks whose `status` is "yes".

### Escalation & effort
Render each `category: "escalation"` check that is "yes" as a
bulleted line — bold trigger, grounded detail, then an italic
pointer to the section carrying the full rule:

- **Cost share / matching required** — 1:1 non-federal match of
  the total award *(see Budget Requirements & Policies)*
- **Limited submission** — maximum of two proposals per
  institution *(see Eligibility)*
- **Documents requiring signature / institution must submit** —
  submitted via Research.gov by the institution's AOR *(see
  Submission Details)*

Add the italic pointer for the financial triggers (cost share,
F&A → Budget), limited submission (→ Eligibility), and
signature/submitter (→ Submission Details). Keep each line to
one sentence.

### Contract Review Unit (CRU) triggers
Render each `category: "cru"` check that is "yes" as a bulleted
line — bold trigger, grounded detail. If ONE OR MORE cru checks
are "yes", add this action line immediately below the subgroup
heading, in bold:

**⚠️ Route to the Contract Review Unit (CRU) before submission —
email the Contract Review Officer via VERAS Correspondence.**

If NO cru check is "yes", omit the entire "Contract Review Unit
(CRU) triggers" subgroup (heading and action line included).

### Empty / clear states
If NONE of the fixed checks (either group) came back "yes",
render exactly this and nothing else in the section:

> ✅ No red flags identified — standard submission process
> expected. Checks performed: cost share; F&A / indirect
> limits; institutional / executive commitment letter; limited
> submission; signature / institution-must-submit;
> indemnification; IP / data ownership; publication
> restrictions; insurance; NDA; FAR / contract-type terms;
> governing law of another state; acceptance of T&C on
> submission; restricted country / foreign ownership; foreign
> government or national-lab contracting; CUI / classified.

When SOME checks are "yes" and others came back "no", after the
rendered flags add one closing italic line naming the notable
checks that were verified clear, e.g.:

*Checked and clear: publication restrictions, indemnification,
restricted-country involvement.*

Do NOT list "unclear" checks as either flagged or clear; omit
them (the underlying sections still carry whatever the document
said). NEVER raise a flag the RISK FLAGS fragment did not mark
"yes".

---

## DATES & DEADLINES

## Placement contract (enforce as you render)

1. **Award amount and duration appear ONLY in AWARD
   INFORMATION.** Even if the budget fragment mentions them,
   do not restate.
2. **Detailed financial rules appear ONLY in BUDGET
   REQUIREMENTS & POLICIES — NOWHERE ELSE (not Award
   Information, not Special Requirements, not Important
   Notes).** This includes cost-sharing / matching
   requirements (source of match, %, cash vs. in-kind), F&A /
   indirect-cost rates and caps (e.g. "indirect limited to
   10% of the total award"), funding limits, and allowable /
   unallowable-cost rules. Do NOT restate, summarize, or
   re-flag these anywhere outside Budget — not even as a
   "critical warning" in IMPORTANT NOTES. If any other
   fragment surfaces a financial rule, render it under Budget
   only.
3. **RED FLAGS is the ONE exception to rule 2 — but only as a
   POINTER.** The Red Flags banner MAY note the PRESENCE of a
   financial trigger (cost share required, F&A limited/waived)
   in one short line with an italic "*(see Budget Requirements
   & Policies)*" pointer. It must NOT reproduce the detailed
   rule (percentages, base, documentation) — that stays solely
   in Budget. The same pointer-only rule applies to limited
   submission (*(see Eligibility)*) and signature / submitter
   (*(see Submission Details)*).
4. **Per-component formatting rules (page limits, fonts,
   naming) appear ONLY on the individual component's Special
   Requirements column** in the APPLICATION COMPONENTS
   table. Not in the top-level SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS section.
5. **Submission mechanics (portal, file format, naming)
   appear ONLY in SUBMISSION DETAILS.**
6. **Mandated-section enumerations appear ONLY in the
   Announcement-Mandated Structure block.** Do not restate
   them in the top-level SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS section, and do
   not compress them into the component's Description cell —
   the table cell carries the one-sentence description plus
   the "See required structure below." pointer.

## Formatting rules

- Preserve the sponsor's monetary formatting verbatim
  (`$1,234,567`, `$0.5M`, `30% MTDC`).
- Preserve dates exactly as stated, including time and
  timezone components.
- Use `**bold**` for labels and critical action items; use
  `*italics*` sparingly for warnings.
- Use `—` (em dash) for empty optional fields in tables;
  "Not specified in the document" for empty required fields.
- No JSON. No code fences around the output. No preamble. No
  closing commentary about the rendering. The output is the
  deliverable — render it as if you were writing the document
  directly.

validation_plan.name: Eleven sections present
validation_plan.description: Verify the Markdown deliverable contains all eleven sections in order (Red Flags, Dates & Deadlines, Eligibility, Award Information, Budget Requirements & Policies, Submission Details, Application Components, Compliance Risks, Foreign Influence & International Components, Special Requirements, Important Notes).

validation_plan.name: Placement contract enforcement
validation_plan.description: Verify each key fact has a clear PRIMARY home and that sections do not CONTRADICT each other: (a) award amount and duration are present in AWARD INFORMATION; (b) the detailed financial rules (cost-share / matching, F&A / indirect, funding limits, allowable costs) are present in BUDGET REQUIREMENTS & POLICIES. The RED FLAGS section is the one deliberate exception: it MAY carry a SHORT pointer to a financial trigger (e.g. "Cost share required — see Budget") without restating the detailed rule, and this pointer redundancy is ACCEPTABLE and must NOT fail. Elsewhere a figure or rule MAY also be referenced in a second section where it is contextually relevant. FAIL only if a primary placement is MISSING (amount/duration absent from Award Information, or the financial rules absent from Budget), or if two sections state CONTRADICTORY values for the same fact.

validation_plan.name: Monetary amount preservation
validation_plan.description: Verify monetary amounts preserve the sponsor's original currency formatting (dollar signs, commas, basis annotation).

validation_plan.name: Eligibility completeness
validation_plan.description: Verify both Eligible Institutions and Eligible Individuals subsections are present and non-empty.

validation_plan.name: Red Flags section grounded
validation_plan.description: Verify the RED FLAGS section renders and that every flag raised traces to a concrete statement in the announcement (escalation flags: cost share, F&A limit/waiver, commitment letter, limited submission, signature / institution submits; CRU triggers: indemnification, IP / data ownership, publication restrictions, insurance, NDA, FAR / contract terms, governing law of another state, acceptance of T&C on submission, restricted country / foreign ownership, foreign-government / national-lab contracting, CUI / classified). FAIL if a flag is asserted with no supporting basis in the document, or if the section is omitted entirely. When any CRU trigger is "yes", the "route to the Contract Review Unit via VERAS" action line must be present.

validation_plan.name: Compliance & International sections grounded
validation_plan.description: Verify the COMPLIANCE RISKS and FOREIGN INFLUENCE & INTERNATIONAL COMPONENTS sections render, that only "yes"/"no" areas appear (never "unclear"), and that each rendered area traces to a concrete statement in the announcement. FAIL if a compliance obligation or international restriction is asserted without a supporting basis in the document.

validation_plan.name: Mandated internal structure enumerated
validation_plan.description: When the announcement enumerates named sections that must appear inside a proposal component (most often the Project Description — e.g. "All proposals should clearly include sections for each of the following aspects:"), verify the deliverable renders a "Required structure" block under APPLICATION COMPONENTS listing EVERY mandated section by its announcement name, including enumerated sub-parts (numbered sub-sections, required table columns, named milestones). FAIL if the enumeration is replaced by a pointer to the announcement (e.g. "must include all subsections listed in Section V.A") or if named sections are missing. PASS trivially (no block expected) when the announcement mandates no internal structure — the block must then be absent, not rendered empty.
